purpose: Determine whether the historical BERT 512-token input limit materially changes the report-level comparison or removes impression-like sections.

analysis.eligible_rows: Reports with one unique report key, nonblank report text, and all five Reference Annotator labels in {1,2,3,4}.
analysis.truncation_exposure: An eligible report is exposed when untruncated bert-base-uncased tokenization contains more than 512 tokens, including special tokens.
analysis.section_check: For exposed reports only, locate line-leading Impression, Interpretation, Conclusion, or Clinical Correlation headings without reading model outcomes; record whether the first such heading begins beyond the retained 512-token character boundary.
analysis.primary_sensitivity: For each cohort, model, and category, compare the complete eligible population with the common population after excluding every BERT-truncation-exposed report.
analysis.interpretation_rule: Report exact affected counts and all metric changes. Do not call a small change equivalence, and do not infer that an unrecognized section heading was absent. The sensitivity addresses BERT input truncation, not patient independence or clinical validity.

prohibited: excluding reports from the primary historical record
case selection based on labels or model correctness
report text or report key release

governed: input hashes and exact analysis configuration
